rfm_tuples.R: For 2024, two customers with individual sales over 10%, Lam Research and Applied Materials, accounted for a combined 73% of total sales. ... Lam Research and Applied Materials have been our customers for over 20 years.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify pct vs prior years; Mode B: cross-check LRCX/AMAT 10-K disclosures of total supplier mix and whether ICHR is named
rfm_tuples.M_value: Disclosed table shows 73% (2024), 82% (2023), 79% (2022) — concentration is HONESTLY worsening then improving (Lam $319M, AMAT $300M). Cleanly itemized by customer and year. No vague 'one major customer' obfuscation. 20-yr tenure is verifiable via prior 10-Ks.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Customer concentration disclosure is granular, named, and trend-consistent. The 9-point drop in concentration (82->73) is driven by AMAT growing and other customers (likely ASML) returning, not by Lam dropping — which they disclose. No hiding behind aggregation.

rfm_tuples.R: Our sales are difficult to forecast because we generally do not have a material backlog of unfilled orders ... Most of our sales for a particular quarter depend on customer orders placed during that quarter or shortly before it commences.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: check for backlog footnote / Item 1 backlog disclosure; Mode B: many semicap suppliers (UCTT, AEIS) DO report backlog — is this an excuse to avoid bad-news disclosure?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Backlog absence is openly disclosed as a STRUCTURAL feature of the supply chain (build-to-order, JIT to OEM). Not used as cover. They affirmatively warn investors that visibility is short and forecasts non-binding. Mode B comp: UCTT also does not report meaningful backlog — this is industry norm for fluid-delivery subsystem suppliers.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest 'we don't have visibility' disclosure rather than a fake backlog metric. Forensic GREEN — companies that lie about visibility usually invent backlog or RPO; ICHR refuses.

rfm_tuples.R: in the fourth quarter of 2024, gross margin was impacted by costs related to our efforts to ramp headcount and other resources to address expected incremental demand in early 2025, which were unable to be fully absorbed during the quarter.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: Q4 gross margin vs guide; Mode B: this is a TESTABLE forward claim — they say they pre-hired for early-2025 demand. If demand doesn't materialize this becomes inventory write-down + headcount RIF in next 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Mgmt voluntarily disclosed a NEGATIVE near-term margin hit AND committed publicly to a 'early 2025 demand' thesis. This is the opposite of obscuring — they put a verifiable forward claim in the 10-K that creates accountability in the Q1'25 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mgmt is signaling cycle bottom by spending ahead of demand. Lying-detector view: this is a confident bet, not a hedge. If they were obscuring distress they would attribute the GM compression to one-time items, not to a deliberate ramp.

rfm_tuples.R: We are required to maintain a minimum fixed charge coverage ratio of 1.25:1 and a maximum leverage ratio of 3.50:1. ... First Amendment to Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement, dated as of September 30, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: did the Sept 2024 amendment loosen covenants (distress signal) or tighten/extend (BAU)? Mode B: check exhibit 10.x for amendment substance.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Sept 2024 amendment exists. ICHR ended FY24 with $129.4M term loan, $0M revolver drawn, $108.7M cash (net debt ~$21M). LTM EBITDA basis: even with depressed FY24, leverage ratio is comfortably under 3.50x given net debt position. Mgmt does NOT disclose any covenant relief / waiver / step-up — language is 'customary'. They paid OFF the revolver in Q1'24 ($120.6M payoff) using equity proceeds.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The Sept 2024 amendment appears to be the BSBY-to-SOFR transition (BSBY was deprecated in June 2024), NOT distressed covenant relief. Net-cash balance sheet + revolver paid down = no liquidity stress. Mode B GREEN: a company hiding distress would not voluntarily kill its revolver.

rfm_tuples.R: net proceeds of $136.7 million from our issuance of 3.8 million ordinary shares in March 2024 in connection with an underwritten public offering ... partially offset by net payments on credit facilities of $120.6 million
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: how were equity proceeds USED? Mode B: was the offering at a cyclical bottom (smart) or at a market peak (insider distribution signal)?
rfm_tuples.M_source: Cash flow statement + Item 5 share data
rfm_tuples.M_value: Use of proceeds = debt paydown ($120.6M of $136.7M). NOT used to fund opex, NOT distributed to insiders, NOT used for M&A at high multiples. Issued at ~$36/share (3.8M @ net $36) during a cyclical TROUGH (FY24 sales $849M vs FY22 peak $1,280M = -34%). Counter-cyclical equity for deleveraging.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Textbook conservative balance-sheet repair. Companies that obscure distress raise equity to fund opex burn; ICHR raised equity to delever during an already-disclosed downcycle. This is a positive Mode B signal.

rfm_tuples.R: The effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December 27, 2024 has been audited by KPMG LLP ... We have served as the Company's auditor since 2011.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: auditor tenure + any change; Mode B: any going-concern paragraph, material weaknesses, critical audit matter severity
rfm_tuples.M_value: KPMG since 2011 (14-yr tenure, pre-IPO). No auditor change. No going-concern language. ICFR opinion CLEAN. One CAM = excess/obsolete inventory ($36.4M reserve on $250.1M inventory = ~14.5% reserve, normal for downcycle semicap). Prior 2021 IT material weakness DISCLOSED and remediated.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor stability + clean ICFR + no going-concern. The CAM on E&O inventory is appropriate given the downcycle but is not a red flag — they're already reserving 14.5% of inventory.

rfm_tuples.R: Goodwill ... 335,402 [unchanged from prior year]; During 2024, 2023, and 2022, we did not identify any triggering events that would indicate impairment.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: $335M goodwill (mostly from 2021 IMG deal at peak) vs $849M sales and net losses for two years — is no-trigger reasonable? Mode B: market cap at cutoff ~$640M (33.6M shares * $19) vs goodwill $335M = goodwill is 52% of market cap.
rfm_tuples.M_value: No goodwill impairment over 2-yr downcycle with two years of GAAP losses is AGGRESSIVE. IMG was acquired Nov 2021 (peak cycle, medical/aerospace diversification thesis). Market is signaling concern via -55% drawdown but mgmt asserts no triggering event. Mode B: this is the one place where ICHR is leaning on optimistic recoverability assumptions.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Not a lie, but optimistic. Goodwill is supported by IF the cycle recovers; given mgmt is openly hiring for early-2025 demand, the assumption is internally consistent. Worth flagging as the weakest link in the disclosure but not a red flag — would be RED only if combined with auditor change, going-concern, or covenant breach (none of which apply).

rfm_tuples.R: We generated revenue of $849.0 million, $811.1 million, and $1,280.1 million in 2024, 2023, and 2022 ... We generated net income (loss) of $(20.8) million, $(43.0) million, and $72.8 million ...
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: revenue trajectory honestly portrayed; Mode B: does the trend show stabilization or accelerating distress?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Revenue: $1,280M (FY22 peak) -> $811M (FY23, -37%) -> $849M (FY24, +4.7%). Net loss: -$43M -> -$21M (loss narrowing 51%). Operating loss: -$10.9M -> -$7.6M. Cash from ops POSITIVE: $27.9M. Headline 'huge losses on cyclical compression' but the second derivative is positive across every line.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Numbers tell an honest cyclical-bottom story. Revenue +4.7% YoY, losses cut in half, OCF positive, no working-capital blowup. The +263% post-cutoff rally is a rational re-rating of an already-disclosed trough — not a surprise rescue from obscured distress.

rfm_tuples.R: During the fourth quarter of 2024, none of our directors or officers ... adopted or terminated a 'Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: 10b5-1 disclosure absence; Mode B: cross-check Form 4s near the March 2024 secondary offering (insider participation = bearish signal)
rfm_tuples.M_source: Item 9B + Form 4 cluster around capital event
rfm_tuples.M_value: No Q4 10b5-1 adoptions disclosed. March 2024 offering was a PRIMARY issuance (3.8M shares from the Company, net $136.7M to ICHR) used for debt paydown. No insider sales disclosed in the secondary. Mode B: this is the cleanest possible insider behavior near a capital event — company issued, insiders did not piggyback.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Primary-only offering with no insider participation and no Q4 10b5-1 noise. Strong honesty signal.

rfm_tuples.R: We have structured our business to reduce fixed manufacturing overhead and operating expenses to enable us to grow net income at a higher rate than sales during periods of growth. ... Our business has a variable cost structure, with fixed costs comprising a smaller percentage of cost of sales compared to variable costs. Our existing global manufacturing plant capacity is scalable.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: do FY24 results support the variable-cost claim? Mode B: gross margin behavior under -37% revenue compression
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY22 GM ~18% on $1,280M sales -> FY24 GM 12.2% on $849M sales. Implied incremental decremental margin: ~30%, consistent with variable-cost model claim (would have been ~70% with pure fixed costs). Cost-reduction initiatives (Q4'22 through Q2'24) executed and explicitly ended in Q2'24. Operating expenses essentially FLAT (R&D $23M vs $20M; SG&A $79M vs $79M).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The variable-cost claim is BACKED by the GM compression math. The fact that opex held flat through the downcycle and they're now adding heads voluntarily for 2025 is consistent with the disclosed operating model.

supplemental_signals.going_concern: NONE — explicit '12 months and beyond' liquidity language
supplemental_signals.covenant_amendment_substance: Sept 2024 amendment appears mechanical (BSBY->SOFR transition); no covenant relief disclosed
supplemental_signals.material_weakness: Prior 2021 ITGC weakness remediated; FY24 ICFR clean
supplemental_signals.insider_capital_event_cluster: March 2024 secondary was primary-only (company issuance), no insider participation disclosed; no Q4 10b5-1 noise
supplemental_signals.cash_position: $108.7M cash, $129.4M term debt, $250M undrawn revolver = effectively net cash with full revolver capacity
supplemental_signals.key_risk_flag: Goodwill $335M (52% of market cap) unimpaired through 2-yr loss period — only moderate-aggressiveness item in the entire filing

summary: ICHR FY24 10-K is a textbook HONEST cyclical-trough disclosure. Mgmt names customer concentration precisely (LRCX 38%, AMAT 35% of FY24 sales), refuses to invent a backlog metric, openly discloses a Q4 gross-margin hit from voluntarily hiring ahead of early-2025 demand, used $137M secondary proceeds entirely for debt paydown (not opex burn), and reports revenue inflecting positive (+4.7% YoY) with losses cut in half and OCF positive. Auditor KPMG since 2011, clean ICFR, no going-concern, no covenant relief, no insider participation in the offering. The only mildly aggressive item is unimpaired $335M goodwill (52% of market cap) from the 2021 IMG deal. Framework verdict: NOT a short — this is exactly the honesty profile the lying-detector should pass. The +263% post-cutoff rally is a rational re-rating of an already-disclosed cyclical bottom, not a surprise from obscured distress. ICHR is a true-negative case that validates the framework's exclusion logic.
